text: Before the experience I was in a constant state of fight or flight. My job in sales was very high pressure, and I was drinking six or seven coffees a day and barely sleeping. During the experience I had a strong physical sensation of my nervous system finally relaxing, like a muscle that had been clenched for years letting go. I hadn't known that was possible. Since then I've been trying to get back to that state. I reduced the coffee, I started going to bed at a fixed time, and when I feel the adrenaline rushing during a stressful call, I put my hand on my chest and breathe slowly. I also changed jobs eventually, to something with less pressure. I'd say my ability to handle stress has improved enormously, partly because I handle it better and partly because I've removed some of the causes.

Ich habe weniger Angst vor schwierigen Gesprächen und kann sie ruhiger führen. Neulich musste ich einem Mitarbeiter kündigen, und ich bin erstaunlich gelassen geblieben, obwohl mich so etwas früher tagelang beschäftigt hätte.

I realised during the experience that I tend to see every problem as a catastrophe because that's what my mother did. Every little thing was a drama in our house. When I notice myself doing that now, I can stop and ask: is this really a catastrophe? Usually it isn't.
Its helped a lot, I'm way more chill

Die Erfahrung hat mir geholfen, belastende Lebensereignisse in einem größeren Zusammenhang zu sehen. Ich bin religiös erzogen worden, habe mich aber schon lange vom Glauben entfernt. In der Erfahrung hatte ich ein starkes Gefühl, dass es eine Ordnung gibt, die größer ist als ich. Das ist kein Gott im klassischen Sinne, eher ein Vertrauen in das Leben selbst. Wenn heute etwas Schlimmes passiert, wie die Krankheit meiner Mutter oder die Arbeitslosigkeit meines Mannes, dann gerate ich zwar auch in Sorge, aber ich habe dieses Grundvertrauen, dass wir das durchstehen werden und dass auch schwierige Zeiten einen Sinn haben können. Ich bete sogar manchmal wieder, auf meine eigene Art.

I learned to slow down. When things get stressful, my instinct is to rush and do everything at once, which makes it worse. Now I deliberately slow down, do one thing at a time, and it's much more effective. I learned this during the experience, where time slowed down so much that I could see each moment clearly.
Not changed, I still get stressed easily

Ich bin durch die Erfahrung mit meiner eigenen Verletzlichkeit in Kontakt gekommen, und das hat meinen Umgang mit Stress verändert. Früher habe ich in Krisen immer die Starke gespielt und alles allein gestemmt. In der Erfahrung habe ich gesehen, dass hinter dieser Stärke ein kleines Mädchen steckt, das Angst hat und Trost braucht. Seitdem erlaube ich mir, in schwierigen Zeiten auch Schwäche zu zeigen und Hilfe anzunehmen. Ich rede mit meinem Mann darüber, wenn mich etwas belastet, und ich gönne mir Pausen. Das klingt banal, aber für mich war das eine riesige Veränderung. Ich bin weniger erschöpft und kann besser mit Belastungen umgehen, weil ich sie nicht mehr allein tragen muss.

During the experience I learned how to observe my emotions without being swept away by them. I use that all the time now. When I get anxious before a big presentation, I notice the anxiety, I notice my heart beating faster, and I just let it be there while I do what I need to do. It used to paralyse me, now it's more like background noise. I've also started meditating to practice this, and I think it's made me much better at handling stressful situations in general, not just at work.
I don't get as anxious about work deadlines. I prioritise better.
Ich habe gelernt, dass ich nicht jede Situation unter Kontrolle haben muss. Das hat mir viel Stress genommen, vor allem im Familienalltag mit drei Kindern.

It's been about four years since the experience and I still notice its effects. The most important one for handling stressful events is a sense of perspective. During the experience I went through what felt like my entire life, from birth to death, in a few hours. I saw all my worries, all my fights, all my failures, and they all seemed so small in the end. What mattered was love and the people I'd shared my life with. Whenever I'm in a stressful situation now, I try to imagine myself on my deathbed looking back at this moment. Would it matter? Usually not much. This helps me prioritise and let go of the small stuff. It has been especially helpful in my relationship, where we used to fight about stupid things like dishes and money. Now I just ask, is this worth it? And mostly it isn't, so I let it go. For the big things, like when my father died, it helped me to focus on what really mattered, which was being there for my mother and my siblings, and letting myself grieve.
I'm more okay with failing. Stress used to come from fear of failure, and that fear is a lot less now.
Hat sich nicht wirklich verändert, ehrlich gesagt.

I've stopped using avoidance as a coping strategy. I used to ignore problems until they became crises, unpaid bills, health issues, relationship stuff. The experience made me see that avoiding is actually more stressful than facing things. Now I deal with things as they come, which means I'm less stressed overall. I opened all my unopened letters the week after the trip, which was terrifying but felt amazing afterwards.

The experience was quite frightening and since then I'm actually more anxious in stressful situations. I get a sense of unreality when I'm very stressed, which I didn't have before. It's manageable but annoying.

Ich kann mit Stress besser umgehen, weil ich gelernt habe, auf meine innere Stimme zu hören. Wenn ich merke, dass ich überfordert bin, sage ich das jetzt auch, statt einfach weiterzumachen. Das fällt mir zwar nicht immer leicht, aber ich werde besser darin.
I'm a much calmer parent. My son has autism and meltdowns used to make me panic and shout. Now I can stay calm and be there for him. I learned during the experience to stay present in chaos.

I think the main thing is that I now have a sense of inner safety that I can come back to. I grew up in foster care and I've always felt like the ground could disappear under my feet at any moment. Any change, any conflict, any unexpected bill would make me feel like I was falling. During the experience, I felt held, really held, for the first time in my life, and I felt that this safety was inside me, not something someone else had to give me. It's not always easy to access, but when I'm stressed now I try to find that place. I put my hand on my belly, I breathe, and I remind myself that I'm safe now. This has helped me through some really hard situations in the past year, including a housing crisis and the end of a long friendship. I'm also in therapy, and my therapist says the experience gave us something to build on.
Ich bin entspannter geworden.

I'm more connected to my community now and I think that has helped me cope with stress. I joined a men's group after the experience and we meet every two weeks. Having people to talk to about what's going on in my life has made stressful things feel so much more manageable. I didn't realise how isolated I was before.
Stress at work doesn't touch me in the same way. I do my job and I leave it there. My identity isn't tied to it anymore.

Mir ist durch die Erfahrung klar geworden, dass ich bei Stress immer sofort in Selbstvorwürfe verfalle. Das passiert immer noch, aber ich merke es schneller und kann mich dann bewusst davon distanzieren. Ich sage mir dann innerlich: Stopp, das ist der alte Film. Das hilft erstaunlich gut.
I have more patience with myself and others when things don't go as planned. I used to be very rigid, now I'm more flexible.
Honestly I don't know. The experience was more about having fun with friends than anything therapeutic.

Ich habe durch die Erfahrung gelernt, die Dinge nicht so schwer zu nehmen. Ich war früher sehr ernst und habe mir über alles Gedanken gemacht. Seitdem lache ich mehr, auch über mich selbst, und das macht vieles leichter. Wenn heute etwas schiefgeht, kann ich oft darüber schmunzeln, statt mich tagelang zu ärgern. Das hat auch meinen Freunden und meiner Familie gutgetan, die meinten, ich sei viel lockerer geworden.

I deal with stress by going into nature now. It's like the experience reconnected me with the forest and the sea, and when I'm stressed I go there and it resets me. I've also started bouldering, which forces me to focus on the moment.

I used to have a lot of panic attacks under stress. The experience made me realise that the panic was not dangerous, just uncomfortable. During the trip I had a massive panic attack and I survived it, I even laughed at the end. Since then I'm not afraid of panic anymore, and funnily enough I've had way fewer panic attacks. When I feel one starting I just say, okay, here you are again, and it usually passes quickly.
Belastende Ereignisse kann ich besser verarbeiten, weil ich weniger grüble.
I see the people who cause me stress differently. I have more compassion for them, because I see that they're struggling too. That makes it easier not to take it personally.

I've realised that I'm a highly sensitive person and that a lot of my stress comes from overstimulation. During the experience everything was so intense, sounds, lights, emotions, and I suddenly understood that this is a heightened version of how I experience the world every day. That was a revelation. Since then I've been much better at managing my energy. I wear earplugs in loud places, I take breaks from social events, I don't schedule too much in one day. I don't feel guilty about it anymore. This has made a huge difference, I'm less exhausted and I can handle stressful events much better when I'm not already overstimulated.
Ich bin seitdem viel ruhiger, wenn es Streit in der Familie gibt. Früher bin ich sofort mit eingestiegen, heute kann ich mich auch mal raushalten und abwarten.
Nothing changed in that area for me.

Since the experience I deal with stress in a more mature way. I think before, I acted like a child when things got hard. I'd sulk, blame others, or run away. The experience made me see myself from the outside, and I didn't like what I saw. Now I try to take responsibility for my reactions and I communicate better with the people involved. I've had a lot of stressful events in the last two years, my company went through layoffs, my partner and I bought a house, and I've handled it all much better than I would have before.

Ich bin achtsamer geworden und merke früher, wenn mir etwas zu viel wird. Dann nehme ich mir Zeit für mich, mache einen Spaziergang oder rede mit einer Freundin. Das hilft mir, nicht in eine Überforderung zu rutschen.
A lot less anxious about money and the future. I used to worry constantly, now I trust it will work out.

I think the main change is that I'm better at sitting with uncomfortable feelings. I used to distract myself immediately with my phone, food, or TV whenever I felt stressed or anxious. During the experience, I couldn't distract myself, I had to sit with everything that came up, and it was the most intense thing I've ever experienced. But it also showed me that feelings pass if you let them. Now I try to sit with my stress for a bit before reaching for a distraction. It's not easy and I don't always manage, but I'm getting better at it, and I feel like I'm actually dealing with things instead of just pushing them away.
Leider habe ich danach eine Weile lang stärker auf Stress reagiert. Mittlerweile hat sich das wieder normalisiert.
I'm better at handling stress because I'm not so hard on myself. When I make a mistake at work, I don't spiral into self-hatred anymore. I just fix it and move on.

The experience taught me that I'm not alone. I used to feel completely isolated in difficult times, like nobody could understand me. During the experience I felt connected to everyone and everything, and since then I've been reaching out to people more. When my brother was in the hospital last year, I called my friends and let them support me. I've also become better at supporting others when they're going through hard times.
